inputs.root_cause: Event 172's citation audit found IPYNB-DOCMETA-001 (title/authors) and IPYNB-HIDDEN-001 (source_hidden/outputs_hidden) cite a metadata-adapters test file whose fixtures never touch those four fields, and confirmed model/metadata.py had no typed representation for any of them at all -- a real gap, not a mis-citation, needing new production code.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: New AuthorMetadata and JupyterCellMetadata dataclasses plus title/authors/jupyter accessors on NotebookMetadataAdapter/CellMetadataAdapter in model/metadata.py, exported through model/__init__.py and the top-level package. 9 new tests (4 positive, 5 negative-path parametrize cases) in test_obligation_metadata_adapters.py. All 4 obligations promoted to implemented.

execution_steps: 1. Read all 4 obligations' exact rule_text from plans/strategic/ff6/obligations/ipynb.yaml. Two are 'schema delta' framings (SAL fact text describing what the pinned nbformat schema says), two are the actual behavioral modeling requirements.

2. Read the pinned, vendored nbformat JSON schemas at src/python/ipynb/src/format_factory/ipynb/validation/schemas/nbformat.v4.2.schema.json and nbformat.v4.3.schema.json directly (not from memory, per GAP-008) to confirm the exact intended shapes: metadata.title (string), metadata.authors (array, each item's shape declared under the non-standard 'item' keyword rather than 'items' so never schema-enforced, item shape {name: string, additionalProperties: true}); cells[].metadata.jupyter.source_hidden (boolean, declared for raw/markdown/code cells) and .outputs_hidden (boolean, code cells only) -- both also declared as siblings of additionalProperties rather than nested under a properties key, so likewise never schema-enforced.

3. Read model/metadata.py in full to learn its established pattern: frozen dataclasses with a _raw field, a from_value classmethod using shared _mapping/_required_string/_optional_string helpers, an .extras property computed by subtracting a known-keys frozenset, and a .to_dict() returning a defensive copy. Added an _optional_bool helper following the same shape as _optional_string.

4. Added AuthorMetadata (name: str | None, extras preserving every other author field, matching the schema's unenforced-but-intended item shape) and JupyterCellMetadata (source_hidden, outputs_hidden: both bool | None, extras preserving unknown jupyter keys). Wired title/authors onto NotebookMetadataAdapter and jupyter onto CellMetadataAdapter, updating each adapter's extras known-keys set.
5. Exported both new classes through model/__init__.py and format_factory/ipynb/__init__.py's import and __all__ lists, matching the existing KernelSpecMetadata/LanguageInfoMetadata export pattern.

6. Verified interactively before writing tests: a two-author fixture (one with name+extra field, one with only an unrelated field and no name) round-trips correctly with both name and extras handled per-item; a code cell with source_hidden/outputs_hidden/an unknown vendor key round-trips correctly; an authors entry that is not a mapping raises MetadataShapeError.

7. Extended the shared _document() fixture in test_obligation_metadata_adapters.py with title/authors and cell-level jupyter metadata, added 4 new dedicated positive tests, and extended the existing test_malformed_known_metadata_fails_explicitly parametrize list with 5 new negative cases (malformed title, malformed authors container, malformed individual author item, malformed jupyter container, malformed source_hidden type).

8. Ran ruff and mypy on all 3 changed source files (clean) and the full ipynb suite (707 passed, was 698) before writing any evidence claim, then ran the skills-first resolve/manifest/receipt/closeout sequence since src/ was touched, then patched the evidence YAML and ran the reconciler.

evidence.oracle: The intended author-item and jupyter-visibility field shapes are read directly from this package's own pinned, vendored nbformat JSON schema files (validation/schemas/nbformat.v4.2.schema.json, nbformat.v4.3.schema.json), not from memory. The typed model's behavior for those fields is otherwise SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per GAP-008, not independently cross-checked against nbformat's own Python validator for these specific new fields.
evidence.obligations_moved_breakdown: All 4 promoted to implemented via genuinely new production code (2 new dataclasses, 3 new adapter properties) plus 9 new tests (4 positive, 5 negative), closing both of event 172's remaining IPYNB-DOCMETA-001/IPYNB-HIDDEN-001 deferred clusters in one slice.
evidence.closes_event_172_deferred_clusters: This slice closes the last 2 of event 172's 3 deliberately-deferred clusters (IPYNB-DOCMETA-001, IPYNB-HIDDEN-001); IPYNB-PRESERVE-001 was already closed at event 173.
evidence.schema_delta_finding: Both obligation pairs turned out to describe the same underlying schema quirk: the pinned nbformat schema uses a non-standard singular keyword ('item' for authors, and top-level sibling placement for jupyter.source_hidden/outputs_hidden) that a real JSON Schema validator does not enforce. The typed model intentionally does not over-constrain beyond what the schema actually enforces (name and both hidden booleans are all optional, extras always preserved), documented directly in each obligation's implemented_behavior and in AuthorMetadata/JupyterCellMetadata's own docstrings.
